```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(fpp3)
```

## Time and Tsibbles

retail_ts is monthly U.S. retail sales from FRED, SA and NSA, index Month, key series_id. can_gas is monthly Canadian gas production from fpp3, one series so no key, index Month.

```{r}
retail_raw <- read_csv("data/retail_sales_raw.csv")
head(retail_raw)
```

2.2a date. it guessed right

```{r}
retail_raw <- read_csv(
  "data/retail_sales_raw.csv",
  na = ".",
  col_types = cols(
    observation_date = col_date(format = "%Y-%m-%d"),
    RSAFS = col_double(),
    RSAFSNA = col_double()
  )
)
```

2.2b set the types so it doesn't guess. na = "." since fred uses a period for missing values

```{r}
retail_raw_long <- retail_raw |>
  select(observation_date, RSAFS, RSAFSNA) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = c(RSAFS, RSAFSNA), names_to = "series_id", values_to = "sales")

head(retail_raw_long)
```

2.3a wide is one row per month with a column per series. long stacks them, 834 rows with series_id and sales

```{r}
retail_ts <- retail_raw_long |>
  mutate(Month = yearmonth(observation_date)) |>
  as_tsibble(index = Month, key = series_id)

head(retail_ts)
has_gaps(retail_ts)
```

2.4b [1M] means monthly. no gaps in either series

```{r}
head(canadian_gas)
key_vars(canadian_gas)
index_var(canadian_gas)
```

2.5a only one series so no key. index is Month

```{r}
can_gas <- canadian_gas |>
  select(Month, Volume)

has_gaps(can_gas)
head(can_gas)
```

2.5b no gaps

```{r}
can_gas_recent <- can_gas |>
  filter(Month >= yearmonth("1990 Jan"))

head(can_gas_recent)

can_gas_recent <- can_gas_recent |>
  mutate(year = year(Month),
         month = month(Month, label = TRUE),
         quarter = quarter(Month))

can_gas_recent |>
  as_tibble() |>
  group_by(month) |>
  summarize(avg_volume = mean(Volume))
```

2.6b Dec is highest, June is lowest

```{r}
can_gas_recent |>
  mutate(next_month = Month + 1,
         same_month_last_year = Month - 12) |>
  head()
```

2.6c +1 is next month, -12 is same month last year

```{r}
can_gas_q <- can_gas |>
  filter(Month <= yearmonth("2004 Dec")) |>
  index_by(Quarter = yearquarter(Month)) |>
  summarize(Volume = sum(Volume))

head(can_gas_q)
can_gas_q |> autoplot(Volume)
```

2.6d it's a total so you add up the 3 months. still seasonal, winter quarters are higher

```{r}
retail_ts |> autoplot(sales)
```

```{r}
retail_ts |>
  autoplot(sales) +
  labs(
    title = "U.S. Retail and Food Services Sales",
    subtitle = "Seasonally adjusted vs. not seasonally adjusted",
    x = NULL, y = "Millions of dollars", color = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

2.7b NSA spikes every December and drops in Jan. SA doesn't. long run they move the same, same trend and recessions. SA just removes the seasonal part

```{r}
can_gas |>
  autoplot(Volume) +
  labs(
    title = "Monthly Natural Gas Production in Canada",
    subtitle = "January 1960 - February 2005",
    x = NULL, y = "Billions of cubic meters"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
can_gas |>
  autoplot(Volume) +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE, color = "red") +
  labs(
    title = "Canadian Gas Production with a Loess Trend",
    x = NULL, y = "Billions of cubic meters"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

2.7d added a red trend line with geom_smooth to see the trend better

## Transformations

3.1a not really. they grow until the 80s then get smaller after

```{r}
can_gas <- can_gas |>
  mutate(log_volume = log(Volume))

can_gas |>
  autoplot(log_volume) +
  labs(title = "Log of Canadian Gas Production", x = NULL, y = "log(Volume)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

3.1b trend is smoother but swings are now bigger early and smaller late. logs are ok but don't fix everything

```{r}
retail_nsa <- retail_ts |>
  filter(series_id == "RSAFSNA") |>
  mutate(log_sales = log(sales))

retail_nsa |>
  autoplot(sales) +
  labs(title = "NSA Retail Sales", x = NULL, y = "Millions of dollars") +
  theme_minimal()

retail_nsa |>
  autoplot(log_sales) +
  labs(title = "Log of NSA Retail Sales", x = NULL, y = "log(sales)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

3.1c stronger for retail. swings stay the same size after logging

```{r}
can_gas <- can_gas |>
  mutate(
    growth_direct = 100 * difference(Volume) / lag(Volume),
    growth_logdiff = 100 * difference(log_volume)
  )

can_gas |>
  autoplot(growth_direct) +
  labs(title = "Monthly Growth Rate of Canadian Gas Production", x = NULL, y = "Growth rate (%)") +
  theme_minimal()

can_gas <- can_gas |>
  mutate(growth_gap = abs(growth_direct - growth_logdiff))

can_gas |>
  autoplot(growth_gap) +
  labs(title = "Gap Between Direct and Log Difference Growth Rates", x = NULL, y = "Percentage points") +
  theme_minimal()

summary(can_gas$growth_gap)
```

3.2a approximation is really close, gap is usually under 0.3 points. only off in big months

```{r}
retail_ts <- retail_ts |>
  group_by_key() |>
  mutate(growth_mom = 100 * difference(log(sales))) |>
  ungroup()

retail_ts |>
  autoplot(growth_mom) +
  labs(
    title = "Month-over-Month Growth: SA vs. NSA Retail Sales",
    x = NULL, y = "Growth rate (%)", color = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

3.3 NSA is way noisier because it still has the seasonal pattern. SA has it removed

## Seasonality

```{r}
retail_ts |>
  filter(series_id == "RSAFSNA") |>
  gg_season(sales) +
  labs(title = "Seasonal Pattern in NSA Retail Sales", y = "Millions of dollars") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
retail_ts |>
  filter(series_id == "RSAFS") |>
  gg_season(sales) +
  labs(title = "Seasonal Pattern in SA Retail Sales", y = "Millions of dollars") +
  theme_minimal()
```

4.1b NSA years all have the same shape with a december spike. SA is flat. so SA is NSA without the seasonal pattern

```{r}
can_gas |>
  gg_season(log_volume) +
  labs(title = "Seasonal Pattern in Canadian Gas Production", y = "log(Volume)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

4.1c high in winter, low in summer. makes sense since gas is used for heating

```{r}
can_gas |>
  gg_subseries(log_volume) +
  labs(title = "Subseries Plot: Canadian Gas Production", y = "log(Volume)")
```

4.2 same thing, Dec and Jan highest, summer lowest. trend goes up in every month

```{r}
retail_nsa_x13 <- retail_ts |>
  filter(series_id == "RSAFSNA") |>
  model(x13 = X_13ARIMA_SEATS(sales)) |>
  components()

retail_nsa_x13 |> autoplot()

retail_nsa_x13 |>
  as_tibble() |>
  mutate(month = month(Month, label = TRUE)) |>
  group_by(month) |>
  summarize(avg_seasonal = mean(seasonal))
```

4.3a December, about 15% above trend. swings get smaller over time

```{r}
sa_compare <- retail_nsa_x13 |>
  as_tibble() |>
  select(Month, mine = season_adjust) |>
  left_join(
    retail_ts |>
      filter(series_id == "RSAFS") |>
      as_tibble() |>
      transmute(Month, census = sales),
    by = "Month"
  ) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (log(mine) - log(census)))

sa_compare |>
  ggplot(aes(x = Month, y = pct_diff)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    title = "My X-13 Seasonal Adjustment Minus the Census Bureau's",
    x = NULL, y = "Difference (%)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

summary(sa_compare$pct_diff)
```

4.3b really close, usually within 0.15%. biggest gaps are in Januaries after covid

```{r}
can_gas_fit <- can_gas |>
  model(TSLM(log_volume ~ trend() + season()))

report(can_gas_fit)

can_gas_fit |>
  tidy() |>
  select(term, estimate, std.error, statistic, p.value) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

4.4a about 0.4% growth per month. June is most significant (t = -4.78)

```{r}
can_gas_fit |>
  augment() |>
  ggplot(aes(x = Month)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = log_volume, color = "Actual")) +
  geom_line(aes(y = .fitted, color = "Fitted")) +
  labs(title = "Linear Trend + Seasonal Dummies Fit: Canadian Gas Production",
       y = "log(Volume)", color = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
```

4.4b fits ok in the middle but misses early and after 2000 when production levels off

```{r}
can_gas_fit |> gg_tsresiduals()

can_gas_fit |>
  augment() |>
  features(.innov, ljung_box, lag = 24)
```

4.4c not white noise. ACF stays really high. Ljung-Box p ≈ 0 so reject

## Forecast Evaluation

```{r}
gas_cv_fc <- can_gas |>
  select(Month, Volume) |>
  stretch_tsibble(.init = 240, .step = 1) |>
  model(snaive = SNAIVE(Volume),
        tslm = TSLM(log(Volume) ~ trend() + season())) |>
  forecast(h = 1)

gas_cv_fc |>
  accuracy(can_gas, measures = list(MAE = MAE, RMSE = RMSE)) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

5.1a Jan 1980 to Feb 2005. SNAIVE MAE 0.562 RMSE 0.702, TSLM MAE 4.01 RMSE 4.36. SNAIVE is better, both agree

```{r}
errs <- gas_cv_fc |>
  as_tibble() |>
  left_join(as_tibble(can_gas) |> select(Month, actual = Volume),
            by = "Month") |>
  mutate(e = actual - .mean) |>
  select(Month, .model, e) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = .model, values_from = e) |>
  na.omit()

forecast::dm.test(errs$snaive, errs$tslm, h = 1, power = 1)
```

5.2a DM = -31.28, p ≈ 0. SNAIVE is significantly better

```{r}
gas_cv_fc_roll <- can_gas |>
  select(Month, Volume) |>
  slide_tsibble(.size = 240, .step = 1) |>
  model(snaive = SNAIVE(Volume),
        tslm = TSLM(log(Volume) ~ trend() + season())) |>
  forecast(h = 1)

gas_cv_fc_roll |>
  accuracy(can_gas, measures = list(MAE = MAE, RMSE = RMSE)) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

5.3a SNAIVE stays the same, TSLM improves to MAE 2.09 RMSE 2.42. dropping old data helps since the trend isn't a straight line

## Reflection

residuals still had a lot of autocorrelation, not white noise. the model misses that the trend and seasonality change over time. that's why it forecast worse than SNAIVE. a better model would let those change or use past values/errors.
